events.what: Huang and Peng prove every oriented graph has a vertex u with |N++(u)| >= 0.715538|N+(u)|
Glover claims a full proof of the general conjecture via the 'Graph Level Order' framework
events.credibility_reason: F5 signals together: landmark problem with no expert uptake in ~20 months; same-topic silence (arXiv:2607.18047, July 2026, says the conjecture 'remains open for general oriented graphs' without flagging the claim); claim's own history of 14 revisions and self-publication via personal site and GitHub; while later specialist work (2606.30588) proves only the out-degree-7 case.

events.what: Sadhukhan, Sandeep and Sen prove the conjecture for oriented graphs with minimum out-degree 7

judgement.doubts: Codes agree with the record. Glover's claim is set aside as not_credible rather than merely a dispute; the record's competing reading (status claimed) is rejected. The out-degree-7 proof relies on OR-Tools CP-SAT checks, a constraint solver, not AI (F9). Huang-Peng bound is a lower tier and does not affect status.
